recipes.title: Freeman House Chai Concentrate (Copycat)
recipes.description: Ginger forward, demerara sweetened, restrained spice blend (no vanilla, star anise, fennel, or nutmeg).

items: 2 inch piece fresh ginger (about 30g), sliced and smashed
10 to 12 green cardamom pods, cracked open
1 tsp whole black peppercorns, lightly crushed
4 to 5 tbsp loose Assam CTC tea (or 5 Assam tea bags)
**Prep spices:** Crack cardamom pods, lightly crush peppercorns, slice ginger into 1/8 inch coins and smash, break cinnamon into pieces.
**Toast:** Dry toast cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and peppercorns over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant. Don't skip.
**Simmer:** Add water and ginger. Bring to a boil, then cover and gently simmer 25 to 30 minutes.
**Sweeten:** Stir in demerara sugar while hot until dissolved.
**Steep tea:** Off heat, add tea. Cover and steep exactly 5 minutes. Don't squeeze bags.
**Strain and store:** Strain, cool to room temp, bottle, refrigerate.

notes: Assam CTC tea gives the malty backbone. Fresh ginger is non-negotiable. Turbinado can sub for demerara.
Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated (best in 7 to 10 days). Freeze in ice cube trays up to 3 months.
Bitter? Tea over-steeped or boiled. Flat? Increase ginger 50%.
Dirty chai: add a shot of espresso. Stronger spice: simmer 40 minutes before adding tea. Less sweet: 2 to 3 tbsp sugar.

extras.title: Serving
extras.body: 1 part concentrate to 1 part milk (oat milk works great). Heat until steaming (don't boil) or pour over ice.

items: 4 to 5 black tea bags (or 3 tbsp loose Assam)

extras.title: Latte ratio
extras.body: 1 part concentrate to 2 parts oat milk (go 1:1.5 for stronger).

items: 2 to 3 tbsp evaporated milk (or half-and-half or coconut cream)
Brew tea mix in boiling water 5 minutes. Strain through fine mesh or cloth.
Stir in condensed milk while hot.
Pour over a tall glass of ice.
Top with evaporated milk. Don't stir, let it cascade.

extras.title: Street style move
extras.body: pour back and forth between cups to aerate before serving.

recipes.title: Hot Toddy

items: 4 to 6 oz hot water, just off boil (or lemon ginger honey tea)
Optional: cinnamon stick, 2 cloves, slice of fresh ginger
Honey in the mug first, dissolve with a splash of hot water.
Add lemon juice and whisky, top with remaining hot water.
Garnish with a lemon wheel and spices.

notes: Add whisky after steeping so you don't cook off the alcohol. Using lemon ginger honey tea as the base is an upgrade.

extras.title: Ratio (3-2-1)
extras.body: 3 parts prosecco, 2 parts bitter liqueur, 1 part soda water. Over ice with an orange slice.

extras.title: Liqueur options
extras.body: Aperol (sweeter, lower ABV), Campari (more bitter and boozy), Select (traditional Venetian, in between), Cynar or Contratto (adventurous).

recipes.title: Reed's Style Extra Strong Ginger Beer

items: 12 to 16 oz fresh ginger (3 to 4x a normal recipe)
Juice of 3 to 4 lemons or limes
1/4 cup ginger bug liquid OR 1/4 tsp champagne yeast
Grate or food process ginger (skin on). Boil in 4 cups water 15 to 20 minutes.
Off heat, add sugar, honey, and cayenne. Steep 1 to 2 hours (or overnight). Strain, pressing the pulp hard.
Add citrus juice and remaining 4 cups cold water. Cool to room temp.
Add ginger bug or champagne yeast.
Bottle in pressure-rated flip-top bottles, 1.5 inches headspace. Ferment 3 to 4 days at room temp, burping twice daily.
Refrigerate once very fizzy. Let it sit 3 to 5 days in the fridge before drinking.

extras.title: Safety
extras.body: This much sugar creates serious pressure. Burp bottles and refrigerate promptly.

ingredients.name: Ginger bug (5 to 7 days)
items: 2 to 3 inches fresh ginger, unpeeled, grated

steps.name: Ginger bug (5 to 7 days)
items: Combine in a jar, cover with cloth.
Each day add 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 tbsp sugar, stir.
Ready when bubbly and yeasty smelling.
Feed weekly at room temp or every 2 weeks refrigerated.

steps.name: Ginger beer
items: Boil ginger in 4 cups water 10 to 15 minutes. Add sugar, steep 30 to 60 minutes.
Strain. Add lemon juice and remaining 4 cups cold water. Cool to room temp.
Stir in ginger bug liquid. Bottle with 2 inches headspace.
Ferment 2 to 4 days at room temp, burping daily. Refrigerate once fizzy. Drink within 2 to 3 weeks.

recipes.title: Fluffy Pancakes

items: 1 tbsp butter or oil for the pan
Whisk dry ingredients in one bowl, wet ingredients in another.
Pour wet into dry and stir just until no dry streaks remain. Lumps are fine.
Rest batter 5 minutes while the pan heats.
Heat nonstick skillet over medium-low, add butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and edges set (about 2.5 minutes).
Flip once, cook about 1.5 minutes more. Hold in a 200°F oven on a rack.

notes: Buttermilk swap: 1.25 cups buttermilk, reduce baking powder to 1 tsp and add 1/2 tsp baking soda.
Don't press pancakes after flipping. Medium-low heat is the move.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Cornbread Waffles (Johnny Cakes Inspired)
recipes.description: A riff on Jeni's discontinued Johnny Cakes flavor, with toasted oat crumble and lemony blueberry preserves.

items: Preheat waffle iron to medium-high. Oven to 200°F for holding.
Whisk dry ingredients. Separately whisk buttermilk, eggs, butter, vanilla.
Combine just until no flour streaks. Rest 10 minutes.
Crumble: melt butter in a skillet, add oats, sugar, salt. Toast 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden. Cool on a plate.
Warm preserves until loose, stir in lemon juice and salt. Don't cook it down.
Cook waffles (1/2 to 3/4 cup batter each) 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden. Hold on oven rack.
Plate: preserves, fresh blueberries, crumble, maple syrup. Pat of butter optional.

notes: Use fine cornmeal, not coarse polenta. Make crumble same day. Optional scoop of vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche.

recipes.title: McDonald's Fruit and Maple Oatmeal (Copycat)

items: 1 tbsp maple syrup (plus a tiny drop of maple extract, optional)
Cook oats with water and salt about 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in brown sugar, maple, and cream.

notes: Toss apples in a little lemon juice and a pinch of cinnamon for brightness.

ingredients.name: Cookie dough
items: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temp
2 tbsp finely ground espresso (real grind, not instant)
**Cornflakes:** Melt butter and brown sugar in a skillet until bubbling. Add cornflakes, toss 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Cool on parchment, rough chop into clusters.

**Dough:** Cream butter and sugars 3 to 4 minutes. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla. Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, ground espresso, and espresso powder separately. Combine until just mixed. Fold in 3/4 of the cornflakes.
**Rest:** Refrigerate at least 1 hour (overnight is better).
**Bake:** 375°F. Scoop 2 oz balls, press reserved cornflakes on top. Bake 10 to 12 minutes until edges set and centers look slightly underdone.
**Finish:** Flaky salt immediately out of the oven.

recipes.title: Bakery Cookie Skillet
recipes.description: For reheating a store-bought bakery cookie into a skillet dessert.

items: Place cookie in a small oven-safe skillet (6 inch cast iron ideal). Optionally preheat the empty skillet 1 minute for a toasted bottom.
Add a few pats of butter and extra chocolate chips. Drizzle 1 to 2 tsp milk or cream over the top.
Warm at 300 to 325°F for 5 to 8 minutes until edges crisp and center goes soft.
Optional: broil 30 to 60 seconds for crisp edges (skip for thin, crispy cookies).
Top with vanilla ice cream and a pinch of flaky salt. Serve from the hot skillet.

recipes.title: Pan de Muerto
recipes.description: Soft, buttery, orange-scented sweet bread for Día de Muertos (Nov 1–2), topped with crossed dough "bones" and a coat of sugar.

ingredients.name: Dough
items: 3 large eggs plus 2 yolks, room temp
1 tbsp orange blossom water (agua de azahar)
1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened and cubed

ingredients.name: Topping
items: 1/2 cup sugar, rubbed with a little orange zest
**Infuse:** Warm the milk with the anise seeds until steaming. Steep 10 minutes, strain, and cool to lukewarm (about 100°F).
**Mix:** In a stand mixer, combine flour, sugar, yeast, salt and orange zest. Add the milk, eggs, yolks and orange blossom water. Mix on low 5 minutes until a shaggy dough forms.
**Butter:** On medium, add butter a few cubes at a time. Knead 10 to 12 minutes until smooth, glossy and elastic. It will be soft and tacky, so resist adding much flour.
**First rise:** Cover and let rise somewhere warm 1.5 to 2 hours until doubled. (Or refrigerate overnight; cold dough is much easier to shape.)
**Divide:** Set aside about 1/5 of the dough (around 150g) for decorations. Split the rest in half and shape each into a tight, smooth ball. Place on a parchment-lined sheet and flatten slightly.
**Bones:** From the reserved dough, roll 2 small marbles for the skulls. Roll the rest into 4 ropes about as long as the loaves are wide. Press with spread fingers as you roll to make knobby "bones."
**Decorate:** Brush the loaves with egg wash. Lay 2 bones across each loaf in an X, then press a skull ball in the center. Brush again to glue everything down.
**Second rise:** Cover loosely and let rise 45 to 60 minutes until puffy. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
**Bake:** Brush gently with egg wash. Bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and 190°F inside. Tent with foil around 20 minutes if browning fast.
**Finish:** Cool 10 minutes. Brush all over with melted butter and sprinkle heavily with orange sugar.

notes: No orange blossom water? Use 1 tsp vanilla plus extra orange zest.
Keeps 2 days wrapped at room temp. Refresh 5 minutes in a 300°F oven.
Serve with Mexican hot chocolate, champurrado, or a latte made with the Freeman House chai.

recipes.title: Jamaican Brown Stew Oxtail (5 lb Practice Batch)
recipes.description: From the Oxtail Off competition prep. This is the home scale practice version. The full 28 lb competition recipe, shopping list, and day-of timeline live in the source chat.

ingredients.name: Braise and finish
items: 1/4 cup light brown sugar (for blackened sugar)
Onion, garlic, ginger, scallions (split into two halves)
1 whole scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice berries, bay leaves

ingredients.name: Spinners
items: 1 cup AP flour, 1 tsp salt, about 1/3 cup water
**Prep:** Rinse oxtail in cold water with a splash of vinegar or lime. Pat completely dry.
**Marinate:** Combine marinade, add oxtail, massage 5 minutes. Refrigerate 24 hours (48 preferred).
**Dry:** Pull oxtail, reserve marinade. Pat each piece dry.

**Blackened sugar:** Heat Dutch oven over high, add 1/4 cup brown sugar. Stir until nearly black and smoking (about 5 minutes). Carefully add 2 tbsp boiling water (it splatters). Stir into a dark syrup.
**Brown:** Add oxtail in 2 batches, coat in caramel, brown about 10 minutes per batch. Remove. Pour off all but 2 tbsp fat.
**First aromatic add:** Half the onion, garlic, ginger, scallions, plus whole scotch bonnet, half the thyme, allspice, bay leaves. Stir 5 minutes.
**Braise 1:** Return oxtail, juices, and reserved marinade. Add stock and water to almost submerge. Bare simmer, covered, about 1 hour (300°F oven or low stovetop).
**Second aromatic add:** Remaining aromatics, 2 tbsp white sugar, 1 tbsp browning.
**Braise 2:** About 1 more hour until meat is loose on the bone. Test at 45 minutes.
**Spinners (during braise 2):** Mix flour, salt, water into a firm dough. Knead 2 minutes, rest 30 minutes. Roll about 12 tapered 2 inch cylinders.
**Pull and strain:** Cool oxtail 15 minutes. Strain sauce through a fine mesh strainer, skim fat hard.
**Debone:** Pull meat in rustic chunks. Don't shred.
**Reduce:** Reduce sauce on medium-high until visibly thicker (about 15 minutes).
**Spinners in:** Simmer 18 to 22 minutes until cooked through with no chalky center.
**Finish:** Add butter beans and meat back to the sauce. Thicken with a flour slurry (flour whisked into hot braising liquid) about 15 minutes before serving.

extras.title: Key moves
extras.body: long marinade, blackened sugar, two-stage aromatics, strained glossy sauce, Pickapeppa and browning over Worcestershire.

extras.title: Competition Plating Options
extras.body:
Presentation ideas for the same braise, from the competition plating chat.

- **Pressed terrine (recommended):** Pack warm deboned meat into molds while still saturated with braising liquid. The gelatin sets it. Slice thick medallions, sear for bark, glaze with the reduction.
- **Short rib style:** Pull meat in the largest chunks possible. Stack 3 to 4 pieces vertically in a ring mold, glazing between layers. Height wins on competition plates.
- **Dumpling:** Wrap deboned meat in wonton wrappers or dumpling dough. Pan fry for a crispy bottom, steam the top. Serve in a shallow pool of reduced braising liquid.
- **Croquette:** Shred meat, bind with reduced braising liquid, form cylinders or balls, bread in panko or fine cornmeal, deep fry. Serve on scotch bonnet aioli or jus.

**Finishing touches**
- Scotch bonnet oil: blend scotch bonnet with neutral oil, then strain. Color and heat without chunks.
- Fresh thyme sprig across the top, thinly sliced scallion greens, a few whole pimento berries on the plate for aroma.

**Scaling note:** For big batches, braise in two pots rather than one giant one. Even consistency matters more than time saved.

recipes.title: Jerk Spiced Duck Tacos (Bon Appétit)
recipes.description: Build-your-own tacos. Low and slow roast renders the fat and makes the meat fall-apart tender.

items: 16 habanero chiles, stems removed (keep the seeds; the duck fat tames the heat)
2 pieces (2 inch) ginger, scrubbed and crushed
**Score:** With a clean razor blade or very sharp thin knife, cut through the skin and fat but not into the flesh. Salt generously. Place each duck in a large resealable bag.
**Marinade:** Finely grind allspice. Add to a blender with finely grated nutmeg, habaneros, soy sauce, rum, vinegar, and sugar. Purée smooth.
**Marinate:** Divide marinade between the bags, add ginger to each. Seal, press out air, work the marinade around. Refrigerate breast side down 12 hours.
**Roast:** About 300 to 325°F for 5 hours. Drain fat every 45 to 60 minutes.

notes: Keep the ducks whole (don't butterfly) so they self-baste.
The roast yields 2+ cups of habanero spiced duck fat. Save it for plantains or potatoes.
Pairs well with pickled onions, cilantro, lime, and a cooling slaw.

extras.title: Timeline from frozen (5pm dinner)
extras.body:
- 3 days before: move ducks from freezer to fridge.
- Night before: score and start the 12 hour marinade.
- Day of: into the oven by about 12pm.

recipes.title: Mexican Style Flank Steak Tacos (Stovetop + Oven)

items: 1 tsp dried oregano (Mexican if you have it)
Whisk everything from olive oil through cilantro into a marinade.
Marinate steak 2 hours minimum, ideally 4 to 8. Max 12 hours.
Rest at room temp 30 minutes. Preheat oven to 400°F. Pat steak dry.
Sear in smoking hot cast iron 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Move skillet to oven 4 to 7 minutes. Pull at 130°F (medium-rare) to 135°F (medium).
Char tortillas over a gas flame 15 to 20 seconds per side. Wrap in a towel.
Slice thin (1/4 inch) against the grain on a slight bias.
Double up tortillas, add steak, onion, cilantro, lime. Salsa on the side.

notes: Deeper flavor: swap soy for 1 tbsp soy plus 1 tsp Worcestershire.
Smokier: add 1 minced chipotle in adobo plus 1 tsp adobo sauce to the marinade.
Extra toppings: pickled red onion, queso fresco, radish, avocado, salsa macha.

recipes.title: Short Rib Bulgogi

items: 2 lb thinly sliced boneless short rib
1/2 cup grated Asian pear (about half a pear)
1/2 yellow onion, grated or thinly sliced
If not pre-sliced, freeze meat 30 to 45 minutes, slice 1/8 inch against the grain. Pat dry.
Whisk everything except green onions into a marinade.
Marinate at least 30 minutes, up to overnight. Not much past 24 hours (the pear turns it mushy).
Sear in batches in a nearly smoking cast iron or grill, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Don't crowd.
Top with green onions and sesame. Serve with rice, lettuce wraps, kimchi, or ssamjang.

notes: Bone-in LA galbi works with the same marinade, just grill a bit longer.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Daeng Gai)

items: 3 tbsp Thai red curry paste (Mae Ploy or Maesri)
**Crack the coconut cream:** Heat oil, add coconut cream, stir 3 to 4 minutes until it splits and oil separates.
Fry curry paste in it about 2 minutes until fragrant and darker.
Add chicken, cook 3 to 4 minutes until no longer pink outside.
Add coconut milk, bring to a gentle boil. Add lime leaves, fish sauce, sugar. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add bamboo shoots and pepper, cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Off heat, stir in basil, top with chilies. Adjust with fish sauce or sugar. Serve over jasmine rice.

extras.title: Variations
extras.body:
(from the Gaeng Phet version in the Rolodex build chat)
- Beef: flank steak, simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
- Shrimp: add at the end, 3 to 4 minutes.
- Vegetarian: firm tofu, mushroom stock, light soy in place of fish sauce.
- Duck: leftover roast duck added at the end with the basil. Good use for jerk duck leftovers.
- Balance check: more salt, add fish sauce. Too salty or spicy, add sugar. Flat, squeeze of lime.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Khiao Wan Gai)

items: 150g Thai eggplant, quartered (or Japanese eggplant, cubed)
100g pea eggplant or green beans, trimmed
Crack coconut cream in oil, 3 to 4 minutes until glossy and oil separates.
Fry curry paste 2 minutes. Add chilies, toss briefly.
Add coconut milk, lime leaves, fish sauce, sugar, eggplant. Simmer 10 minutes.
Off heat, stir in basil and lime juice. Adjust seasoning. Serve with jasmine rice or roti.

notes: Red and green share most of the same base, so both can be made together as a dinner spread.

recipes.title: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)

items: 6 oz chicken thigh or shrimp, bite-sized
Break up cold rice by hand. (Fresh rice: spread on a sheet pan, refrigerate uncovered 1 hour.)
Heat wok on highest heat, oil until just smoking.
Sear protein 60 seconds untouched, stir-fry until cooked. Remove.
Garlic and shallot 15 seconds. Push aside, scramble eggs into large curds.
Add rice, press flat, let it char. Toss every 30 seconds for 2 to 3 minutes.
Return protein. Add fish sauce, soy, sugar, white pepper. Toss 30 seconds. Add tomato and scallions, toss briefly.
Serve with lime, cucumber, chilies. Squeeze lime right before eating.

notes: Small batches for wok hei. Golden Mountain seasoning sauce in place of soy for extra authenticity.

items: **Boil chicken** with 1 chopped onion, half the garlic and ginger, thyme, half the curry powder, 1 stock cube, and salt in water to barely cover. Cook through (about 25 minutes). Reserve stock.
**Fry chicken** in half the oil until golden. Set aside.
**Blend** tomatoes, bell peppers, scotch bonnets, remaining onion. Boil to reduce about 15 minutes.
**Fry tomato paste** in remaining oil with remaining garlic and ginger until darkened.

**Build stew:** Add reduced pepper blend, bay leaves, remaining curry powder and stock cubes. Fry on medium, stirring often, until oil rises to the top (20 to 30 minutes). This is the heart of the dish.
**Simmer** with fried chicken and a splash of stock, 10 to 15 minutes.

extras.title: Serve with
extras.body: white rice, jollof, boiled yam, or fried plantain. Freezes well.

items: 2 slices day-old Italian bread, crusts removed
Soak torn bread in milk 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess, keep damp.
Beat egg, add bread, Parm, parsley, garlic, salt, pepper. Add turkey, mix by hand until just combined.
With wet hands, gently roll 1.5 inch balls. Don't pack tight.
**Nonna way:** nestle raw into simmering red sauce, cover, low simmer 25 to 30 minutes without moving much.
**Or:** brown in olive oil 7 to 8 minutes, then finish in sauce 15 minutes.

extras.title: Turkey tips
extras.body: Milk-soaked bread is non-negotiable. Grate in a little fresh onion for juiciness. If using 99% lean breast, add 1 tbsp olive oil to the mix.

recipes.title: Roasted Dumpling Squash with Sage Brown Butter
recipes.description: Sweet dumpling squash has thin, edible skin, so there's no peeling. High-heat roasting caramelizes the edges, then a maple sage brown butter goes on top.

ingredients.name: Squash
items: Pinch of cayenne or chipotle powder
**Heat:** Preheat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the lower third. Line a sheet pan with parchment.
**Cut:** Microwave each whole squash 2 minutes to soften it for cutting. Halve stem to base, scoop out the seeds, and cut into 1 inch wedges along the ridges. Leave the skin on.
**Season:** Toss the wedges with olive oil, salt, pepper, cinnamon and cayenne. Spread out cut side down with space between them.
**Roast:** Roast 15 minutes, flip, then roast 10 to 15 minutes more until tender and deeply browned at the edges.

**Brown butter:** While the squash roasts, melt butter in a small pan over medium. Add sage and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the butter smells nutty and turns golden brown and the sage is crisp. Off heat, stir in maple syrup and vinegar.
**Finish:** Spoon the brown butter and crispy sage over the hot squash. Top with pepitas, flaky salt and cheese if using.

notes: Halves instead of wedges: roast cut side down 30 to 35 minutes, then fill with the brown butter, or stuff with wild rice, sausage or quinoa.
Delicata, carnival or acorn squash all work. Acorn skin is tougher, so add 5 to 10 minutes.
Roast the seeds: rinse, dry, toss with oil and salt, and bake at 325°F for 15 to 20 minutes.
Miso swap: whisk 1 tsp white miso into the brown butter instead of the vinegar.
Good next to the jerk duck tacos, or on the Thanksgiving table.

recipes.title: Nonna's Sunday Sugo (2 Can Version)
recipes.yield: Makes enough for about 1.5 lb pasta

items: 2 (28 oz) cans San Marzano whole peeled tomatoes (DOP)
Hand crush tomatoes into a bowl.
Olive oil over medium-low. Cook onion with a pinch of salt 8 to 10 minutes until soft (don't brown). Add garlic and pepper flakes 1 minute.
Deglaze with red wine, reduce until mostly evaporated.
Add tomatoes plus 1/3 can of water, oregano, half the basil, Parm rind, salt.
Gentle simmer, then lowest heat, lid cracked. Cook 2 hours minimum, stirring every 20 minutes.
Remove rind, stir in remaining basil. Meatballs go in for the last 45 to 60 minutes.
Serve over rigatoni or spaghetti with Pecorino Romano.

extras.title: Making it a day early
extras.body: Cool uncovered 30 minutes, then refrigerate. Reheat low with a splash of water. Hold the final basil until reheating.

recipes.title: Ponzu Sauce

items: 120ml fresh citrus juice (yuzu, or half lemon half lime)
Simmer mirin 30 seconds to cook off alcohol. Cool.
In a jar combine soy, vinegar, mirin, kombu, bonito. No citrus yet.
Refrigerate 24 hours (4 hours in a pinch).
Strain, pressing the bonito. Stir in citrus juice.
Rest 1 hour before using. Adjust to taste.

notes: Keeps 2 to 3 months refrigerated. Great with shabu-shabu, gyoza, sashimi, salads, grilled fish. Same-day shortcut: whisk soy, citrus, mirin, vinegar, and a pinch of dashi powder.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie Spice Blend (No Cardamom)

items: Store airtight in a cool, dark cabinet.

notes: Freshly grated nutmeg is the best upgrade. Potency fades after about 6 months. For a warmer, less sharp blend, cut cloves to 1 tsp and bump cinnamon to 3.5 tbsp.

recipes.title: Kimchi

items: 1 tsp sugar (or rice flour porridge: 1 tbsp rice flour cooked briefly in 1/2 cup water)
**Salt:** Cut cabbage into bite-size pieces. Toss with salt, rest 1 to 2 hours, tossing occasionally. Rinse 2 to 3 times, drain well.
**Paste:** Mix gochugaru, fish sauce, shrimp paste, garlic, ginger, sugar or porridge.
**Combine:** Wearing gloves, massage paste into cabbage, scallions, daikon, carrot.
**Pack:** Press tightly into a clean jar, submerged in its own liquid, 1 inch headspace. Seal loosely.
**Ferment:** Room temp 1 to 3 days, pressing down once or twice daily. Refrigerate once tangy enough.

notes: Use real gochugaru; generic chili flakes won't give the right flavor or color. The rice flour porridge feeds the bacteria for a stronger ferment. Flavor keeps developing in the fridge for weeks.

items: Mound flour, make a well, add eggs, oil, and salt. Work the flour in with a fork, then bring together by hand.
Knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Wrap and rest 30 minutes before rolling and cutting.

extras.title: Practice goal
extras.body: under 15 minutes from start to plate.

items: Toast arborio rice in fat until the edges turn translucent.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring, 18 to 20 minutes until creamy and just tender.
Finish off heat with butter and Parmesan.
